newsitem.title: USA: Vote threatens planned mine plan in Wisconsin.
newsitem.headline: Vote threatens planned mine plan in Wisconsin.

text.p: Opponents of a controversial zinc and copper mine in north-central Wisconsin said Wednesday they had gained ground following a key vote against the project in the state legislature.
The state Senate approved a "mining moratorium" bill by a 29-3 vote and sent the measure to the state Assembly, the legislature's lower house.

The strong bipartisan vote means it will be "very difficult for the Assembly to deny us a hearing and an open vote," said Democratic state Rep. Spencer Black, a major sponsor of the legislation in the Assembly.

Pro-mining forces had hoped the moratorium measure would be killed in the Assembly, which is controlled by Republicans. But now strategists raised the possibility that they'll have to resort to a veto from Gov. Tommy Thompson, who opposes the measure.

Activists both for and against the proposed Crandon Mining Co. project watched as senators cast their votes Tuesday. Crandon Mining is a joint venture of Exxon Coal and Minerals, a division of Exxon Corp, and Canada's Rio Algom Ltd..
The mine would be located in the headwaters of the Wolf River, a popular fishing and whitewater rafting venue that flows through the Menominee Indian reservation southwest of Green Bay.
Supporters of the moratorium said they had momentum after the Senate action because the bill retained its key provisions and because of the larger-than-expected victory margin.

Thompson has proposed a scientific study and rule changes instead of the mining moratorium, but his alternative has not diluted support for the moratorium. He has said the state's present mining laws the toughest in the country.

Under the moratorium bill, Crandon Mining and future mines would have to show, before being developed, proof of a similar mine elsewhere that had operated pollution-free for 10 years and then caused no pollution for another decade after closing.
